messages:
alex: Heads-up — FinReg POC kickoff tomorrow. They cannot accept PrivateLink (vendor appliance is on their side), so customer asks for peering/TGW pattern. Need network preflight + egress controls.
maria: Got it. Do we have a recommended minimal topology for 'no-privatelink' enterprise POC? They want isolation and predictable egress IPs.
jonathan: Yes — recommend a hub-and-spoke with a transit gateway in our private VPC or a dedicated edge proxy fleet. High-level:
jonathan: - Customer VPC(s) <-> TGW peering (or VPC peering if single account) -> Redwood Private VPC
jonathan: - Use NAT Gateway or an outbound proxy in our edge subnet to present static egress IPs
jonathan: - Route tables: send 10.0.0.0/16 (customer) -> TGW attachment, default 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT/edge-proxy
jonathan: Example route table rule snippet:
jonathan: ```
jonathan: Customer-VPC-RT: 10.1.0.0/16 -> local
jonathan: 0.0.0.0/0 -> tgw-attach-0123 (or nat-01a2b3)
jonathan: ```
maria: What about security groups / firewall rules? Customer requires least-privilege outbound and L4 firewall allowlist.
jonathan: Keep SGs narrow: outbound only to our edge proxy on 443. From edge proxy to Redwood control plane/serving endpoints allow:
jonathan: - TCP 443 to 52.38.120.0/22 (example egress pool) — we will provide final CIDR(s)
jonathan: - TCP 22 only if they request an SSH bastion (but prefer no admin SSH in POC)
jonathan: For on-prem vendor appliance talking to our endpoints, they should only need HTTPS egress; enforce SNI allowlist if using TLS inspection-proof flow.
sam: Pricing/POC ops Q: If we front with a NAT or proxy in Redwood, do we charge egress data transfer like Hosted? Also does Dedicated billing change for this topology?
alex: Short answer: egress data transfer follows cloud provider rates plus our Hosted Private egress add-on if we manage the proxy. For Dedicated/Private customers on-reserved capacity, network egress is typically passed through; we'll need to estimate monthly TB to provide a cost bucket. I'll loop finance.
maria: Customer also has a security questionnaire — they want to know if we can provide static IPs and cert pinning guidance. Can we produce an answer doc quickly?
jonathan: Yes. We can provide:
jonathan: - Static egress IPs via NAT/Elastic IPs on proxy
jonathan: - TLS certs: use mutual TLS or client certs on the vendor side if they require mTLS; otherwise provide CA-signed certs and recommend SNI/TLS inspection exemptions
jonathan: Quick checklist to send them:
jonathan: ```
jonathan: 1) Confirm TGW vs VPC Peering (scale + cross-account)
jonathan: 2) Provide customer-owned CIDRs and on-prem egress IP ranges
jonathan: 3) Open outbound 443 to our egress CIDRs
jonathan: 4) Decide on NAT IPs vs managed proxy (proxy gives better observability/control)
jonathan: 5) If using proxy, share TLS SNI and ALPN expectations
jonathan: ```
netops-bot: Reminder: run net-allowlist tool to generate ephemeral test IPs — https://internal.tools/net-allowlist
sam: For the POC timeline: can netops provision a small proxy + 2 egress IPs in 48 hours once we have CIDRs? Customer wants smoke tests and curl -> /v1/health.
jonathan: Yes, we can spin up a small autoscaling edge-proxy ASG, attach 2 EIPs, and push a minimal NAT/proxy policy. Need customer CIDRs and account IDs.
alex: Action items:
alex: - maria: collect customer CIDRs, vendor appliance details, security questionnaire sections by EOD
alex: - jonathan: draft runbook for TGW vs peering + config snippets and sample SG/route rules
alex: - sam: ask finance for a rough egress estimate template to share with customer
alex: Let's sync after you have those; we can schedule a 30m handoff with FinReg netops tomorrow.
maria: I'll send the questionnaire answers and a short network diagram in a follow-up message. :thumbsup:
jonathan: Also note: if customer insists on non-public routing without TGW, we can do VPC peering but won't scale to >5 VPCs easily. TGW preferred for enterprise POC.
sam: Great — I'll block the call and add customer and their vendor ops.
alex: Thanks all. Filing this as the network preflight for the POC.
